title: A common filtered cardinal for a combinatorial Quillen adjunction
statement: Use the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] and the filtered-cardinal and presentability conventions of [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalences-accessible]. An object is $\lambda$-presentable when its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. A Quillen adjunction is an ordinary adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations; trivial means also a weak equivalence. A functorial cofibrant replacement consists of a functor $Q_0$ with a natural trivial fibration $Q_0X\to X$ whose source is cofibrant. A functorial fibrant replacement consists of a functor $T$ with a natural trivial cofibration $Y\to TY$ whose target is fibrant. Let $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$ be combinatorial model categories and let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a Quillen adjunction. There is an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$ and a small full subcategory $\mathcal M_{\lambda}$ of $\lambda$-presentable objects such that: every object of $\mathcal M$ is a small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of objects of $\mathcal M_{\lambda}$; $\lambda$-filtered colimits of weak equivalences in $\mathcal M$ are weak equivalences; $\mathcal M$ has a functorial cofibrant-replacement functor preserving $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\mathcal N$ has a functorial fibrant-replacement functor preserving $\lambda$-filtered colimits; and $R$ preserves $\lambda$-filtered colimits.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i)-(ii), Remark 2.5 and Proposition 3.2 proof, printed pp. 179-182; the right-adjoint preservation clause cites Adámek–Rosický Proposition 1.66.

proof.text: Choose a small set $I$ generating the cofibration/trivial-fibration system of $\mathcal M$, so $I^{\square}=F_{\mathcal M}\cap W_{\mathcal M}$, and a small set $J$ generating the trivial-cofibration/fibration system of $\mathcal N$, so $J^{\square}=F_{\mathcal N}$. The model conventions in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identify the corresponding left classes with $C_{\mathcal M}$ and $C_{\mathcal N}\cap W_{\mathcal N}$. Every member of $I$ or $J$ belongs to its corresponding left class by the definition of the right lifting class. These left classes contain every isomorphism (a square with invertible left map $i$ has filler $ui^{-1}$), are closed under pushouts and arrow retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and are closed under small continuous transfinite compositions by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Consequently they contain the weak saturations of $I$ and $J$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] separately to $(\mathcal M,I)$ and $(\mathcal N,J)$; all Hom sets and colimits are small relative to the fixed universe. This gives functorial factorizations with middle-object functors $E_I,E_J$, preserving small $\kappa_Q$-filtered and $\kappa_T$-filtered colimits, respectively, for infinite regular $\kappa_Q,\kappa_T$. Their right maps are, respectively, trivial fibrations and fibrations, and their left maps are, respectively, cofibrations and trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i), expanded through Proposition 7.1, printed pp. 180 and 193; both accessible factorizations are the existing small-object input.

proof.text: Set $Q_0X=E_I(0\to X)$ and $TY=E_J(Y\to1)$. The natural factor maps give $0\to Q_0X$ a cofibration and $Q_0X\to X$ a trivial fibration, and give $Y\to TY$ a trivial cofibration and $TY\to1$ a fibration. They therefore give exactly the functorial replacements required. The identity/composition and naturality equations in [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] make these object assignments functors with the stated natural maps. For any nonempty filtered category, a constant diagram at an object $A$ has colimit $A$: any two components of a cocone agree because the indices have a common receiving object, and hence cocones are exactly single maps out of $A$. Arrow colimits are computed on endpoints, as in the same cited node. Thus the functors $X\mapsto(0\to X)$ and $Y\mapsto(Y\to1)$ preserve small filtered colimits. Composing with $E_I,E_J$ shows that $Q_0$ preserves small $\kappa_Q$-filtered colimits and $T$ preserves small $\kappa_T$-filtered colimits. This uses constancy over filtered indices, not preservation of arbitrary colimits by the terminal-arrow functor.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i) from Proposition 7.1; restriction of the two arrow factorizations to initial and terminal arrows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalences-accessible] to $\mathcal M$. Its combinatorial hypothesis is precisely the assumed local presentability and set generation of the two model weak factorization systems; no simplicial enrichment is required. Its conclusion and its definition of accessible subcategory give an infinite regular $\kappa_W$ for which the weak-equivalence full subcategory of $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ is closed under small $\kappa_W$-filtered colimits computed in the ambient arrow category. Since arrow colimits are computed on endpoints, a natural transformation of diagrams that is objectwise a weak equivalence has weak-equivalence colimit whenever its small indexing category is $\kappa_W$-filtered.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(ii) and Proposition 7.3, printed pp. 180 and 194; the ambient arrow-closure theorem is the existing input.

proof.text: Choose an infinite regular $\kappa$ and a small family $\mathcal G$ of $\kappa$-presentable objects generating $\mathcal M$ under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits; these exist by local presentability. Apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] in $\mathcal N$ to each object $LG$, $G\in\mathcal G$. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal N$ is locally presentable. Choose an infinite regular rank $\tau_G$ for each $LG$. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the small family of underlying initial-ordinal sets of the cardinals $\tau_G$, together with the initial ordinal of $\kappa$. This gives an infinite regular $\beta$ strictly larger than every $\tau_G$ and than $\kappa$: each of these sets injects into their disjoint union. If $\eta\leq\beta$ then every $\beta$-filtered category is $\eta$-filtered, directly from the definition. Hence every $G$ and every $LG$ is $\beta$-presentable. Choice here is only over the small family $\mathcal G$ and stays in the fixed universe.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, condition (5), printed p. 183, citing Adamek-Rosicky Proposition 1.66; first part of an explicit proof using ranks of images of a small generating family.

proof.text:
Let $D:K\to\mathcal N$ be any small $\beta$-filtered diagram and let $c:\operatorname{colim}_K RD\to R(\operatorname{colim}_K D)$ be the map induced by applying $R$ to its colimit injections. For every $G\in\mathcal G$, presentability and the ordinary adjunction give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(G,\operatorname{colim}RD)\cong\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(G,RD_k)\cong\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(LG,D_k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(LG,\operatorname{colim}D)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(G,R\operatorname{colim}D).$$
Their composite is $\operatorname{Hom}(G,c)$: on a representative $a:G\to RD_k$, naturality of adjunction sends it to $R(\iota_k)a$. Here is the full detection argument. If $f:A\to B$ induces bijections on Hom from every $G$, present $B$ as a colimit of generators $G_j$. Each injection $b_j:G_j\to B$ lifts uniquely to $a_j:G_j\to A$. Injectivity of Hom from $G_j$ makes these lifts compatible with all diagram arrows. They induce $h:B\to A$, and $fh=1_B$ follows on the colimit injections. Present $A$ by generators as well. For each injection $a'_j:G'_j\to A$, the equality $fhfa'_j=fa'_j$ and injectivity on $G'_j$ give $hfa'_j=a'_j$; thus $hf=1_A$. Apply this to $c$. It follows that $R$ preserves small $\beta$-filtered colimits. This is an ordinary Hom argument and does not use a simplicial mapping-space theorem or assume accessibility of $R$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, condition (5), printed p. 183; explicit adjunction and generating-colimit argument replacing the bare reference to Adamek-Rosicky Proposition 1.66.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] to $H=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$ with $\mathcal A=\mathcal D=\mathcal M$ and $\alpha=\aleph_0$. The identity preserves every colimit, so the required accessibility hypothesis holds. The node gives a regular $\rho$ and arbitrarily large infinite regular sharp upper ranks at which $\mathcal M$ is locally presentable. Use its existence clause with $\sigma=\rho$ to choose such a rank $\lambda$ larger than $\rho,\beta,\kappa_Q,\kappa_T,\kappa_W$. A finite maximum of these small cardinal bounds is still a small bound. Then $\mathcal M$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable. A small $\lambda$-filtered diagram is also $\beta$-, $\kappa_Q$-, $\kappa_T$- and $\kappa_W$-filtered, since each diagram with fewer than any of those cardinals' morphisms has fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms. Therefore the already chosen $Q_0,T,R$ preserve these colimits, and such colimits of weak equivalences in $\mathcal M$ are weak equivalences. No assertion that local $\kappa$-presentability persists at every larger regular cardinal is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, simultaneous choice in conditions (1)-(5), printed p. 183; suitable ordinary presentability enlargement uses the existing rank theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-canonical-density] to $\mathcal M$ at the rank $\lambda$ from Step 6. It says that the full subcategory $\mathcal P_\lambda$ of all $\lambda$-presentable objects is essentially small, and that its canonical comma diagrams are $\lambda$-filtered and colimiting. Choose one actual object from each isomorphism class in $\mathcal P_\lambda$ and take the full subcategory $\mathcal M_\lambda$ on those representatives. It is small: its objects form a small set and its Hom sets are small. For any $X$, the comma category $(\mathcal M_\lambda\downarrow X)$ is small too, since its objects form the disjoint union of the small sets $\operatorname{Hom}(A,X)$ over the small set of representatives. The inclusion into $(\mathcal P_\lambda\downarrow X)$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective: given $u:P\to X$, an isomorphism $a:A\to P$ from a representative gives the isomorphic object $ua:A\to X$. Transporting cocones along these isomorphisms shows explicitly that the former comma category is $\lambda$-filtered and its value diagram has colimit $X$: a cocone on fewer than $\lambda$ arrows in the former is obtained in the latter and its apex replaced by a representative, and any cocone from the value diagram extends uniquely to the latter by the same isomorphisms. Thus every object is a small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of objects of $\mathcal M_\lambda$. Together with Step 6 and the replacements of Step 2, this establishes every clause of the statement.

source.place: Remark 2.5 (printed p. 181) and Proposition 3.2 proof, condition (1) (printed p. 183); small full representatives and small comma diagrams made explicit.
